text:
Jesper Bratt was the 162nd pick in 2016, and he keeps playing like one of the best passers in the league. He has 21 points in 21 games, 17 of them assists, and an eight-game point streak (2 goals, 8 assists) as the Devils won eight of his last ten.

The goals lag the chances. He has 4 on 5.9 expected goals (the quality of his shots), shooting 8.5% against a usual range of about 10 to 15. That is the opposite of a hot streak: if anything, his scoring line undersells him.

The real story is what happens when he's out there. At five on five New Jersey takes 62.6% of the expected goals with him on, 8.5 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had his impact on chances created in the 98th percentile among forwards last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts him at 10.2 primary shot assists per 60 (94th percentile) with 72% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck.

Heavy.com has him "Closing In on Another Franchise Legend" on the Devils' scoring list. The passes are why; watch whether the shooting catches up.
